title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DELIA HITS THE ROAD
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Delia Montoya, a fifty-seven-year-old train dispatcher from Joliet, Illinois.
For thirty years, she sent trains all over America. She never went anywhere.
Then, at a yard sale, she saw a rusty old motorcycle with a sign: Make an offer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE OFFER
segments.quote: To accomplish great things, we must not only act, but also dream; not only plan, but also believe.
segments.author: Anatole France
lines: Her idea was crazy. Fix it up and ride Route Sixty-Six to the Pacific Ocean.
Her brother Ray laughed. You can't even ride a bicycle.
But on her fridge was a line from the French writer Anatole France:
To accomplish great things, we must not only act, but also dream; not only plan, but also believe.
So she paid three hundred dollars and signed up for riding lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE GARAGE
segments.quote: The place to improve the world is first in one's own heart and head and hands, and then work outward from there.
segments.author: Robert M. Pirsig
lines: The bike would not start. Delia yelled at it and kicked it.
Her riding teacher, Big Lou, handed her a book by Robert Pirsig:
The place to improve the world is first in one's own heart and head and hands, and then work outward from there.
So Delia stopped yelling and cleaned one part each night. In April, the engine roared.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE DRIVEWAY
segments.quote: I travel not to go anywhere, but to go. I travel for travel's sake. The great affair is to move.
segments.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
lines: Then she sat in her driveway for an hour, worrying about rain and flat tires.
Ray read her a line from Robert Louis Stevenson, the man who wrote Treasure Island:
I travel not to go anywhere, but to go. I travel for travel's sake. The great affair is to move.
Delia stopped planning every mile and rolled out of Joliet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE DINER
segments.quote: Travel is fatal to prejudice, bigotry, and narrow-mindedness, and many of our people need it sorely on these accounts.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: In Oklahoma, six bikers in black leather walked into her diner. She grabbed her purse.
Then she remembered Mark Twain:
Travel is fatal to prejudice, bigotry, and narrow-mindedness, and many of our people need it sorely on these accounts.
So she said hello. They were retired dentists from Tulsa. They fixed her chain and checked her teeth.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE DESERT
segments.quote: A journey is like marriage. The certain way to be wrong is to think you control it.
segments.author: John Steinbeck
lines: In the Arizona desert, the bike died. No phone signal. Ninety-eight degrees.
Delia thought of John Steinbeck, who drove across America with his dog:
A journey is like marriage. The certain way to be wrong is to think you control it.
So she stopped fighting the day. A rancher named Rosa gave her a ride and a spare room.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PIER
segments.quote: Life is what we make it, always has been, always will be.
segments.author: Grandma Moses
lines: Six weeks later, Delia rode onto the Santa Monica Pier and saw the Pacific.
She called Ray and read him a line from Grandma Moses, who became a famous painter in her seventies:
Life is what we make it, always has been, always will be.
Ray said, How much was that motorcycle?
Next summer, they ride together. He's on the back.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dream and plan. Fix yourself first. Just go. Say hello. Let go. Make your life.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Dream and plan. Fix yourself first. Just go. Say hello. Let go of control. Make your own life.
I sat on a motorcycle once. It got a flat tire.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
